legal_gdpr_transfer_mechanism: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with EU data residency addendum (Frankfurt); no adequacy decision needed as processing stays in EU

legal_risks.risk: Zoho DPA subprocessor substitution right allows unilateral changes with only 30-day notice — insufficient for Brightline to assess GDPR adequacy of replacement
legal_risks.mitigation: Negotiate DPA amendment: require Brightline consent or right-to-terminate (not just notice) for Tier-1 subprocessors handling EU personal data

legal_risks.risk: Standard SaaS liability cap (~1x annual fees) is below potential GDPR supervisory authority fine exposure (up to 4% global turnover) leaving Brightline underprotected
legal_risks.mitigation: Negotiate separate data-breach indemnity clause uncapped up to GDPR fine exposure; or purchase cyber-liability insurance to cover the gap

legal_risks.risk: Auto-renewal clause may bind Brightline to multi-year term before legal/DPO review of any updated privacy policy or DPA annex
legal_risks.mitigation: Insert 90-day pre-renewal legal review window; any material DPA change restarts the window and allows termination for cause

legal_risks.risk: Brightline's customer data (logistics shipment PII) processed through CRM triggers Article 30 record-keeping and potentially Article 35 DPIA obligations
legal_risks.mitigation: Commission a lightweight DPIA before go-live; document lawful basis (legitimate interest or contract performance) for each data category in the CRM

legal_risks.risk: NetSuite connector (third-party) is not covered by Zoho's DPA — creates unaddressed sub-sub-processor chain under GDPR Art. 28(4)
legal_risks.mitigation: Require Zoho to either absorb the connector vendor as a named subprocessor in its DPA, or Brightline must execute a separate DPA with connector vendor prior to go-live
